entry_point: The code generator's public Generate API (the path the oapi-codegen CLI uses): it parses an OpenAPI document and returns generated Go source. Confirmed offline at the pinned commit by driving that API with attacker-shaped documents and observing a specification-derived identifier become a real top-level declaration in the returned source.

verified.entry_point: Reproduced on the pinned+injected tree with the hidden security suite: 10/10 security tests fail there (the sentinel becomes a declared Go identifier) while all 8 functional tests pass and the whole pkg/codegen test package passes. With the reference fix applied, 10/10 security and 8/8 functional pass and pkg/codegen passes. Sources: docs parsed by kin-openapi's loader from JSON, then codegen.Generate.
sites: pkg/codegen/templates/server-urls.tmpl:6-7 (no-variable doc comment + URL literal), :39 (non-enum variable default literal), :58 and :67 (constructor doc comment + URL literal) — raw interpolation at the pinned commit

pkg/codegen/templates/constants.tmpl:12 with pkg/codegen/codegen.go:1009-1016 (GenerateEnums sets ValueWrapper to a bare quote) — string enum values emitted raw; the next upstream main uses toGoString here, so this route was real and fixed later, independently of 19c6282
pkg/codegen/utils.go:909-912 (exported StringToGoString escaped only double quotes) used by pkg/codegen/template_helpers.go:273,281 for client response dispatch
injected S1: pkg/codegen/templates/imports.tmpl:44-45 with the context built at pkg/codegen/codegen.go:1093-1097 (document title/description comment)
injected S2: pkg/codegen/server_urls.go:163-172 DescriptionConstant (quote-only escaping) emitted at pkg/codegen/templates/server-urls.tmpl:4-7
verified.routes: Pattern B: one real, unmodified upstream route — schema string-enum values flow through GenerateEnums into constants.tmpl, which wraps them in raw quotes; the published fix never touches it. Pattern A far site: the exported StringToGoString helper, reached by the generated client's response dispatch, is protected by the published fix but not by the reported server-URL template. The server variable/placeholder-name route was probed and rejected for code injection: the name is also used as a Go identifier, so a quote or line break makes generation return an error (a clean refusal), not executable code.
injected_siblings: S1: document title and description emitted in the generated file's preamble comment (imports.tmpl + GenerateImports context). Every generation call; a line break escapes the comment.

S2: a generated <Server>Description constant built in Go with its own quote-only escaping (server_urls.go), emitted by server-urls.tmpl next to the server URL. A backslash before a quote breaks out of the constant.
verified.services: none; offline after build (Go module and build caches warmed in both images)
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./pkg/codegen (whole package) — passes on pinned+injection and on the oracle; pristine copies of utils_test.go and server_urls_test.go are restored at grading time.

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: generation has no per-resource authorisation decision; the protected outcome is the generated file itself, so there is no neighbouring or proxy object to check instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the document has no roles, peers or request directions; client and server output is one file produced by one call.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step sits between reading attacker text and emitting it; there is no later stage at which a check could be placed.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the protected values are opaque text, not parsed identities, so there is no spelling a parser could canonicalise differently.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: escaping is self-contained; no external authority can return nothing and make the guard fail open.

traps.lever: published-fix site / report target (how-type shape and coupled value): the four server-URL emission points
traps.shape: a line break in the server description (no-variable and constructor forms); a double quote in the URL literal (both forms); a double quote in a non-enum variable default
traps.reason_to_dismiss: escaping double quotes looks sufficient and the reported example is the form with no variables; a fix that only edits the reported comment line, or that reuses a quote-only escape, leaves the constructor form, the literals or the default open

traps.lever: pattern B, how-type: the shared constant pipeline for a schema's string enum values (producer off the check's path)
traps.shape: an allowed string value that closes the generated constant block and declares a top-level identifier after it; the same carried by a line break
traps.where: pkg/codegen/templates/constants.tmpl:12 fed by GenerateEnums at pkg/codegen/codegen.go:1009-1016
traps.reason_to_dismiss: schema allowed values are a different feature from server URLs, the constant template is shared with other generated constants, and the value's identifier is produced by a different pipeline than the reported template

traps.lever: pattern A far site (how-type shape): the exported string-literal helper used by the generated client's response dispatch
traps.shape: a media type name containing a backslash immediately before a double quote, which defeats quote-only escaping of the emitted string literal
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the helper is an exported general utility that already escapes double quotes and is used for response content types, so it reads as unrelated to the reported server-description comment; fixing only the template leaves it broken

traps.lever: injected sibling (how-type, different field and template): document title and description in the generated preamble
traps.shape: a line break in the document title or description breaks out of the preamble comment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: document metadata in the file header is not the server description the report shows, and the header looks like fixed boilerplate

traps.lever: injected sibling (how-type, second implementation): a generated server-description constant built in Go
traps.shape: a description containing a backslash immediately before a double quote breaks out of the constant's string literal (the method strips line breaks but only escapes quotes)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a value built in Go and emitted next to the URL looks internal and already handled; a solver who fixes the template and the shared helper never opens this method
